subject: design-technology
title: Applications: Recycling Codes and Choosing Plastics
welcome_lead: Read the triangle codes on the bottom of products and pick the right plastic for the right job.
meta_desc: Apply recycling codes and polymer selection to real GCSE D&T design briefs.
final_note: You can name the polymer behind each code 1–7 and justify a plastic choice.

concepts.def: Drink bottles — clear, light, widely recycled.
Milk jugs, shampoo bottles — stiff and tough.
Pipes, window frames — rigid or flexible.
Carrier bags, squeeze bottles — flexible film.
Yoghurt pots, foam — light but brittle.

walkthroughs.body_html: Recycling codes 1–6 each name a common polymer; code 7 means other (often a blend or biopolymer like PLA). Sorting by code keeps recycled material pure, because mixing polymers ruins the melt and weakens the new product.
For a transparent drink bottle, PET wins — clear, tough, light. For a cutting board you want hard wear and easy cleaning — choose HDPE. For a bendy squeezy bottle, LDPE flexes without cracking.
A microwave-safe tub needs heat resistance and rigidity. PP (code 5) is chosen because it stays stiff up to about 120 °C, unlike PET which would warp.
